vt25_the_jar.topic: Nag Hammadi discovery, dating, custody and burial hypotheses

claims.text: Codices found December 1945 at the base of Jabal al-Tarif, east bank of the Nile across from Nag Hammadi; Muhammad Ali broke the jar; his mother used some leaves as oven fuel; Codex I to the Jung Institute; rest in Coptic Museum, Old Cairo

Latest dated cartonnage scrap 348 CE; codices made c.350 and buried in following decades; burial circumstances 'remain unknown'; 46 different tractates; up to 14 scribes; all Coptic (Sahidic, Subakhmimic) translated from Greek; English translation 1977 under Robinson
Codex XIII is leaves removed in antiquity from a thirteenth book and placed inside the cover of Codex VI

Most codices passed to dealer Phokion Tanos; Department of Antiquities retained them; after 1952 revolution declared national property in Coptic Museum; Jung Codex acquired by the Jung Institute via Gilles Quispel, returned to Cairo only in 1975; Robinson English edition 1977 (Brill/Harper & Row), revised 1988

Robinson's discovery narrative (jar, jinn fear, mother burning pages, blood feud) was assembled from interviews from late 1974; versions of 1977, 1979, 1981 differ on who was present; Kasser and Krause 1984 called much of it 'stories and fables'; Goodacre judges Doresse's earlier vaguer account more reliable
Lundhaug and Jenott argue the codices were produced and read by Christian monks, most likely Pachomians, citing cartonnage, colophons and scribal notes

Lewis and Blount argue the cartonnage has no single Pachomian source (looks like a town rubbish heap), Athanasius's letter targeted Arians and Meletians, and the codices may be a wealthy non-monastic owner's grave goods in the Jabal al-Tarif cemetery, comparing Codex Tchacos and Codex Panopolitanus

vt25_sayings_gospels.topic: Gospel of Thomas, Truth, Philip and the dialogue gospels

claims.text: Gospel of Thomas: 114 sayings; prologue 'These are the secret sayings which the living Jesus spoke'; saying 3 'the Kingdom is inside of you, and it is outside of you'; saying 14 'If you fast, you will give rise to sin for yourselves'; saying 113 'the Kingdom of the Father is spread out upon the earth, and men do not see it'; saying 114 Peter: 'Let Mary leave us' (Lambdin)

Greek fragments P.Oxy 1 (shortly after 200), 654 and 655 (mid-3rd c.); Coptic copy shortly before 350; Patterson c.70-80, Cameron late 1st c. likely; Hippolytus Ref. 5.7.20 (222-235) the one incontrovertible testimonium
Goodacre (2012) argues Thomas knew the Synoptics and dates its final form c.135; reviewer finds method subjective
Hippolytus says Naassenes cite a passage from the Gospel according to Thomas and calls them 'impious'
Cyril of Jerusalem (Cat. 4.36): 'The Manichaeans also wrote a Gospel according to Thomas'; books not read in churches should not be read privately

Decretum Gelasianum lists 'the Gospel in the name of Thomas which the Manichaeans use' as apocryphal, names Valentinus and Basilides among heretics, lists 'books of Proverbs ... prefixed with the name of holy Sixtus' as apocryphal; closes with anathema; heading attributes to Damasus, shorter recension to Gelasius
Irenaeus AH III.11.9: Valentinians 'entitle their comparatively recent writing the Gospel of Truth', which 'agrees in nothing with the Gospels of the Apostles'
Gospel of Truth: NHC I,3 and XII,2; homily; Greek 140-180; possibly Valentinus; ignorance as nightmare, Jesus nailed by Error, 'living book' in hearts, rest in the Father

Gospel of Philip: Valentinian anthology (Layton); 'The Lord did everything in a mystery, a baptism and a chrism and a eucharist and a redemption and a bridal chamber'; 'Those who say they will die first and then rise are in error' (Isenberg); kiss passage damaged at the key word; koinonos ambiguity; mostly dated 3rd c.

Dialogue of the Saviour III,5 c.150; Apocryphon of James I,2 100-200 'be filled', warning that the kingdom become a desert within; Thomas the Contender II,7 self-knowledge and renouncing desire; Treatise on the Resurrection: letter to Rheginos, already risen spiritually, resurrection real

vt25_secret_cosmos.topic: Sethian and Valentinian cosmologies: Apocryphon of John and related texts

claims.text: Apocryphon of John (Wisse): 'The Monad is a monarchy with nothing above it'; Yaldabaoth: 'I am a jealous God, and there is no other God beside me'; 'I am the remembrance of the pleroma'; curse on anyone who exchanges these things for a gift or food or drink

Apocryphon of John: four copies (NHC II,1, III,1, IV,1; BG 8502); long (II, IV) and short (III, BG) recensions; composed before c.180; outline Monad, Barbelo, aeons, Sophia acts without consent, Yaldabaoth, archons, Adam animated by stolen power, Eve, counterfeit spirit, Christ as remembrance of Pronoia, five seals

Irenaeus AH I.29 summarises the Barbelo myth: Barbelo, Ennoia, Autogenes, Sophia/Prunicus, Protarchon who says 'I am a jealous God, and besides me there is no one', and rebuts it from Exodus 20:5 and Isaiah 45

Hypostasis of the Archons II,4: Sethian; archons form Adam, spiritual woman escapes leaving Eve, serpent as instructor, Norea burns the ark, Eleleth rescues her, Sabaoth repents; Origin of the World II,5/XIII,2 shares material, perhaps Alexandria late 3rd c.
Thunder, Perfect Mind (MacRae): 'For I am the first and the last', 'I am the whore and the holy one'; MacRae and Taussig doubt the Gnostic label
Trimorphic Protennoia XIII,1: Sethian; Barbelo descends three times as voice, speech, word

Zostrianos VIII,1 longest tractate, ascent with six baptisms, c.200 Alexandria; Allogenes XI,3 ascent to the Unknowable; Porphyry Life of Plotinus 16 names Revelations of Zostrianos and Allogenes; Epiphanius Panarion 39.5.1, 40.2.2 says Sethians and Archontics use books called Allogenes; Plotinus wrote Ennead II.9 against Gnostics

Gnostic Apocalypse of Peter VII,3: living Jesus 'glad and laughing' above the cross; those who call themselves bishop and deacons are 'dry canals'; Second Treatise of the Great Seth VII,2 docetic, patriarchs a 'laughingstock'; Testimony of Truth IX,3 against the Law, martyrdom, water baptism, procreation, and against Valentinians, Basilideans, Simonians

Holy Book of the Great Invisible Spirit III,2/IV,2 Sethian, Seth's race saved by baptism; Apocalypse of Adam V,5 Adam to Seth, Illuminator, thirteen kingdoms, possibly non-Christian; Tripartite Tractate I,5 Valentinian, Logos falls, three kinds of humans, psychics may be saved

vt25_the_whole_library.topic: Catalogue of all 13 codices and tractates

claims.text: Exegesis on the Soul II,6: soul restored through inward prayer and repentance; Eugnostos III,3/V,1 ineffable God and aeons from Immortal Man, reworked into Sophia of Jesus Christ III,4 (and Berlin Codex) as 13 questions with Jesus quoting Eugnostos

Codex V: Apocalypse of Paul (ascent past toll collector and old man in seventh heaven to tenth); First Apocalypse of James (answers to three toll collectors; also in Codex Tchacos); Second Apocalypse of James (discourse and stoning)

Codex VI: Acts of Peter and the Twelve (Lithargoel, renounce possessions, care for poor); Authoritative Teaching (soul's fall and awakening, Platonic Christianity); Concept of Our Great Power (apocalyptic, mid-4th c.); Discourse on the Eighth and Ninth, Prayer of Thanksgiving (scribal note: selected from a larger library), Asclepius 21-29 Hermetic

Codex VII: Paraphrase of Shem (Derdekeas; warns against water baptism); Teachings of Silvanus (generally non-Gnostic wisdom, Christ as teacher); Three Steles of Seth (hymns to Barbelo, ascent-descent liturgy)
Letter of Peter to Philip VIII,2 and Codex Tchacos; Melchizedek IX,1 rejects docetism, Jesus truly suffered; Thought of Norea IX,2; Marsanes X thirteen seals, letters and ascent

Codex XI: Interpretation of Knowledge (one body, no envy of others' gifts); Valentinian Exposition with rites On the Anointing, Baptism A/B, Eucharist A/B; Hypsiphrone fragmentary; Sentences of Sextus XII,1 Christianised Pythagorean maxims, Latin by Rufinus; Prayer of the Apostle Paul on Codex I flyleaf, Valentinian

Creed of 325 opens 'We believe in one God, the Father Almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible' and says the Son 'was incarnate and was made man. He suffered and the third day he rose again'
